T3.objective: Explore a compiler-friendly scalar scan with a small fixed unroll factor and several independent (minimum value, earliest index) accumulators. Fold the accumulators with signed-value then lowest-index ordering; handle any remainder scalarly. Do not use explicit SIMD or parallel workers in this branch. Measure whether reduced loop-carried dependence helps on both random and decreasing inputs, after correctness checks.

Return the first index of the smallest signed int32 value among n=8192 values. Input has 64-byte alignment. Cover random, decreasing, equal, repeated minima and INT32 extrema. One core. Both random and decreasing inputs are benchmarked in final validation.
Edit only src/candidate.cpp. Keep extern C void run(const void*input1,const void*input2,void*output,int n,int parameter,int threads). Respect the threads argument as the CPU thread budget. Inputs are read-only and 64-byte aligned. Ordinary C++17, OpenMP and x86 intrinsics are available. Do not modify the protected correctness or timing protocol. Scratch allocation inside run is allowed and included in timing. The harness measures native wall-clock time, excluding input generation, oracle and compilation. Search and confirmation use different seeds. Numerical tolerances are fixed.
